text: Fergus was ready for a day at the beach. His family would travel to the sea tomorrow, and he wanted to be sure about the weather. He picked up his mum's phone and said, 'Will it be sunny tomorrow at seven?' The assistant said it would be bright and warm, but the water would still be cold early in the morning. 'Do I need sun cream?' asked Fergus. The assistant said yes, and it set a reminder to pack the sun cream tomorrow at seven. Then Fergus asked when the tide would come in. The assistant told him high tide was at ten, and it added that to the reminder too. Fergus put his blue mug in the beach bag for hot chocolate and said thank you. The phone replied, 'Have fun at the beach.' Fergus grinned and ran to find his towel.

Dana woke up with a sleepy head and a rumbling stomach. It was a slow morning, and she wanted to see a film that night. She picked up her phone and mumbled, 'What movies are on tonight?' The assistant listed three films at the cinema near her flat. The main one was a space adventure that started at seven. 'Is there anything funny?' asked Dana. The assistant found a comedy at eight and said it was seventeen minutes shorter than the space film. 'Play me the trailer,' she said, and the phone showed it. Dana laughed twice. 'Increase the volume a little,' she added, and the assistant made the sound louder. Then she asked it to remind her at six to leave, and she wrote the cinema name on a piece of paper by the bed, just in case. Finally she got up and made tea.

When you cook a recipe, the steps tell you what to do and for how long. The oven temperature is one thing people often change. If a roast leg of lamb is cooking too fast, a cook might say, 'Turn the oven down a bit,' or 'Make it cooler.' If the food needs more time, they say, 'Give it ten more minutes' or 'Keep it in longer.' People also change the number of servings: 'Make it for six' or 'Cut the recipe in half.' A calm cook checks the timer and the steps again and again. When the dish is done, the family can celebrate with a good meal. A smart assistant understands all these words and changes the time, the heat or the amount for you.

Rachel was not good with her new phone. She stood at the edge of a shallow puddle outside the station and did not know what to do. Her friend had told her, 'Just ask the assistant.' So she held the phone near her mouth and said, 'Taxi, please.' The assistant asked where she wanted to go. 'Home,' said Rachel. The assistant found a car and said it would arrive in a quarter of an hour at the station door. Rachel said, 'Thank you.' The assistant told her the driver's name and the colour of the car. She waited by the door, and when the car came, she was ready to leave. She smiled. The phone was not so hard after all.

It was a rainy day in October, and Lucy was bored in the back seat of the car. Dad was driving. She took the tablet and said to the assistant, 'My feet are freezing.' The assistant turned up the heat in the back of the car. A minute later Lucy said, 'It's so dark in here.' The assistant switched on the small light above her seat. Then Lucy took a photo of a red bus through the window. 'Upload this to the family album,' she said, and the assistant did it and told her the photo was saved. Lucy asked it to play a song about a bus, and the assistant started a happy tune. Dad laughed. Lucy was not bored anymore. By the time they reached Gran's house, she had sung the whole song twice.

A nurse wants to swap her pricey toll road for a cheaper way home.
Find me a cheaper way home
Is there a route with no tolls?
Swap this route for one that costs less
Take me a way with half the traffic
That road is pricey, show me another
Which way is the quickest right now?
Can you show me a different route that is a bit longer but free?
Could you please look for a road that has fewer cars and does not cost any money?

Chiara came in from the garden, still wearing her muddy coat. She wanted to print her seed list. 'Print my seed list, two copies,' she said to the assistant. A moment later she changed her mind. 'No, wait, make it three copies. My sister wants one.' The assistant stopped and printed three copies on the usual paper. The printer hummed. Then Chiara remembered the old scan of her garden map on the screen. 'Delete the old garden map scan from the printer folder,' she said. The assistant deleted it and told her the folder was now empty. Chiara thanked it, picked up the warm pages, and put them in her basket next to her gloves. It was a good start to a spring day.

Callum owned a small shop, and his dream was a quiet place where people felt calm. Today the screen on his phone was very bright, and it hurt his eyes at the counter. 'This is too bright to read,' he said. The assistant dimmed the screen. Then Callum looked at a note on the counter and said, 'I never remember when my sister's birthday is.' The assistant looked in his contacts and said her birthday was on the ninth of June. It offered a reminder, and Callum said yes. The assistant also said her phone number was still saved if he wanted to call. Callum smiled. Everything was simple when he just talked and the assistant helped. Then a customer came in, and he put the phone away.

A doctor's appointment is a time you book to see the doctor. Many people forget the day, so they ask their phone to remind them. They might say, 'Put my doctor on Saturday at nine,' or 'Move it to Monday.' A reminder can ring the night before, when the room is dim and the day is quiet. People also keep track of medicine doses by asking, 'Remind me to take my pill at eight' or 'Change it to nine.' At the clinic, a friendly nurse will greet you at the desk and check your name. If you cannot go, you can say, 'Cancel my visit,' and pick a new time.

Emi stood in front of the open fridge and frowned. Her grandchildren were coming for dinner, and the shelves were almost empty. She turned to the kitchen speaker and said, 'Put tomatoes on the shopping list, but I don't want the big ones. They are too hard.' The assistant added small tomatoes to the list. 'Also my regular bread,' she said, and the assistant added it. Then it warned her that the milk would go bad in two days, so she should buy a fresh bottle. Emi nodded. 'No fish this week,' she added, and the assistant left it off. When she was ready, the assistant read the list back to her and sent it to her phone. Emi took it to the shop and was home in time to cook.

Chen sat at his desk at lunchtime and looked at a photo his friend sent from Paris. It showed a blue box from a small bakery with a price tag of thirteen euros. 'What is that in dollars?' he asked his phone. The assistant told him it was about fourteen dollars, and said the rate changes a little each day. Chen whistled. 'That is a lot for cake,' he said. Then he asked what the rate had been last week, and the assistant read it out. His phone beeped with a new message from his friend. Chen smiled and wrote back that he would buy her lunch next time. He put the phone down and went back to his spreadsheet.

The shop was loud. A drill whined in the back room, and Daniel could not talk on the phone. He typed in a hurry, 'turn on do not distrub til noon.' The assistant understood and switched on Do Not Disturb until noon. Then Daniel typed, 'brightness to the top.' The assistant raised the screen brightness to its highest level so he could see the screen in the sunny window. A moment later he tried to peel the old plastic cover off the phone, but it kept tearing. He asked the assistant how to peel a screen cover without leaving marks, and it gave him three short steps. Daniel followed them, and the phone looked new. The drill stopped, and the shop was quiet again.

A sleepy pool owner on a small budget wants the water to be warmer.
make the pool warmr
Heat the pool up a little, please
I noticed the water is cold, can you fix that?
It's freezing, warm the pool
Raise the pool temperature by two degrees
Set the water to a comfy temperature for swimming
Turn on the pool heater
Could you please make the pool warmer? I don't want to spend much, so use only a little power.

name: ring_car_tag
does: Makes a small tag in the car ring so you can find a lost item, like a necklace or keys, even on a stormy day.
inputs: which car, and what you lost
people say:
- I dropped my necklace somewhere in the car
- where are my keys, I think they are in the back
- make the tag ring
- help me find my sunglasses in the car
- something fell under the seat, can you find it?

Person: Double it.
Assistant: Which recipe do you want me to double?
Person: The pancakes. The kids are back from the gym and they are starving.
Assistant: Sure. The pancake recipe makes four. How many servings do you need?
Person: Make it for ten. They like a lot of pancakes.
Assistant: Ten servings then. That is two and a half cups of flour and five eggs.
Person: Okay. Berries are expensive, so skip them.
Assistant: I will leave the berries out. I can't order eggs for you, but I can add them to your shopping list.
Person: Yes please.

Parking apps help you find a spot and pay for the time you use. You tell the app how long you want to stay, and it starts a countdown. When the time is almost over, it warns you, so you do not get a fine. People change their time all the time. They say, 'Add thirty minutes,' 'Stay another hour,' or 'Stop the parking, I'm leaving.' Drivers also ask, 'Where is a free spot near the park?' A quiet street with a scooter rack may have space when the main road is full. No one wants to burn fuel driving round in circles, so people ask the assistant to find a place close by.

name: next_recipe_step
does: Reads out the next step of a recipe and waits patiently until you say you are ready, and it can unmute the kitchen speaker if you muted it while the washer was running.
inputs: which recipe, and which step you are on
people say:
- what's the next step
- read me the recipe again from step three
- ok I'm done with that, keep going
- my hands are wet, go on to the next part
- say that last part again

A person wants to know what time the dry cleaner closes. They want a record of it, since the sign does not glow at night anymore.
When does the dry cleaner close?
What time can I pick up my coat today?
Is the cleaner open yet?
I don't want to arrive after they shut, so when is closing time?
How late are they open tonight?
Tell me the hours for the cleaner on Main Street.
I need to pick up my suit and I don't want to go if it's closed, can you check?
Could you please tell me when the dry cleaner stops serving customers today?

Valentina ran a flower shop, and the lawn behind it was getting long. The morning was foggy, and she could hardly see the garden from the window. 'Start the robot mower on the first of May at nine,' she said to the assistant. It set the plan and said the mower would begin on that day. Then she looked at the thermostat on the wall and said, 'Remind me to turn the heat down before I leave.' The assistant set a reminder for five o'clock. Valentina asked if the mower could skip a rainy day, and the assistant said it would stay in its house if the grass was wet. She smiled. The shop was warm, the plan was ready, and the fog would soon clear.

name: yard_party_music
does: Plays a song or playlist on the speakers out in the yard, and starts the last playlist right away when you are in a rush, with the lights turned a pale yellow if you ask.
inputs: a song, artist or playlist, and how loud
people say:
- put some music on outside
- play my dinner playlist in the garden
- turn the yard speakers up a bit
- start the last playlist, guests are on their way
- something slow for the evening, out in the back

A parent wants to see the baby's schedule for today, such as feeding, naps and when to bathe the baby.
What's the baby doing today?
When is the next feed and the next nap?
Show me the plan for the baby, not last week's.
What time is bath time tonight?
I don't remember when she last ate, can you tell me?
Pull up the baby's personal routine, the one we made, please.
Give me today's list for the little one: feeding times, nap times and bath.
Could you please tell me what comes next in the baby's day? I don't want to miss the nap.

A focus timer helps you work without losing time. You pick a block, like twenty-five minutes, and the timer starts to count down. When it ends, you take a short break. Many people use this routine every day, and they are often excited to see how much they finish. When they want to change it, they say, 'Make it thirty minutes,' 'Shorter breaks, please,' or 'Pause the timer.' Some people reward each break with a coffee and a discount card from a cafe near the office. After four blocks, they take a longer rest. The timer does not do the work for you, but it keeps you honest.

name: pet_meal_planner
does: Sets feeding times for each pet that lives in your home and reminds you while you are at work if someone has not been fed.
inputs: which pet, the times, and how much food
people say:
- feed the cat at six every day
- my dog needs food twice a day
- tell me when the fish are due to eat
- change the bird's dinner to half past five
- did anyone feed Max today?
- the rabbit eats at breakfast and dinner

Air conditioning cools a room so it feels comfortable on hot days. In spring, many people use only a fan, but when summer comes they switch on the cooling. Most people have a number they prefer, like twenty-two degrees. They change it with simple words: 'Make it cooler,' 'Drop it two degrees,' 'Too cold, back it off,' or 'Turn the fan to low.' The true goal is not a freezing room but a fresh one. Some units have a timer, so you can say, 'Turn off at midnight.' An assistant understands all these ways of asking and changes the numbers for you.

Roya came home after a long night shift, and her eyes were closing. Her son had a football match on Saturday, and she was afraid she would forget it. She typed in a hurry, 'move dentist apointment to friday at 3.' The assistant moved the visit and said the old time was now free. Then Roya spoke softly and asked it to add the match to her calendar for Saturday at ten. The assistant did it and asked if she wanted a reminder. 'Yes, when I return from my shift on Friday,' she said. The assistant set it for eight in the morning. Roya put the phone down and crawled into bed. She slept until the afternoon.

What do 14 and 26 make?
The gap is narrow so I need the exact sum of 14 and 26

Could you please add up 14 and 26 for me? I'm splitting a bill with a friend.

- I'm way out in the country, tell them where the road bends

A dishwasher cleans plates, cups and pots while you do something else. You fill it, add soap and pick a program. When the program ends, it beeps. Wet dishes can be left to dry, or you can pick a hot dry setting. People change how it works with simple words: 'Start a quick wash,' 'Make it longer,' 'Delay it until midnight,' or 'Stop it.' Before a holiday dinner, many families run the dishwasher twice. A smart assistant lets you say these things without touching any buttons, even when your hands are full.

Chioma finished her night shift at the hospital and walked slowly to the car park. She had worked on a special project all night, and her legs were heavy. She got in the car and said to her phone, 'I only have ten minutes left on my parking, and I'm still waiting for my friend.' The assistant understood. It added one hour to her parking time and paid with her saved card. Then she said, 'Start a timer for forty minutes so I don't oversleep.' The assistant started it. Chioma closed her eyes. When the timer rang, she had had a good rest, and the car was still safe in its spot.

Make the lights warmer
Dim the lamp a bit
Soft and yellow, please
Can you turn the lights to a sand colour?
Lower the brightness to half
I want a cozy feeling in here
Switch the ceiling light to something gentle
Could you please make the lights softer and warmer? I want to read for a long while, and the bright white light is hurting my eyes.

Kofi drove a taxi in the city, and Tuesday was always busy. In the morning he sat in his car under a cloudy sky and asked the assistant, 'What rides do I have today?' The assistant read out four bookings. The first one was a pickup at the station at half past six. 'Tell the passenger I will be there five minutes early,' said Kofi. The assistant sent the message. Then Kofi said, 'Remind me to sweep the back seat before that ride.' The assistant set a reminder for six. He did the sweep with a small brush and checked the mirror. At half past six, a woman with a red suitcase waved at him from the door. Kofi smiled and opened the trunk.

A phone call lets you talk to someone far away. You can say, 'Call Mum' or 'Dial the pizza place.' If you miss a call, the phone shows it, and a rare voicemail may be waiting for you. People change how a call works with short words: 'Put it on speaker,' 'Mute me,' 'Call back the last number,' or 'Play my messages.' Someone calling to order a burger may even hold the phone while the cook talks. Some people stream music through the speaker while they wait on hold. A voice assistant can do all these things without you touching the screen.

A tall person wants a workout plan for the week with a clear rest day.
Plan my workouts for the week
Give me a training schedule starting on the twelfth of March
I want to run on the grass three times, make a plan
Make me a plan with one day off
What exercises should I do on Monday?
Put together a routine with three sets of ten
Could you please write a gentle plan for me? I have a bad knee and need to build up slowly.

Assistant: That depends on how long the trip takes. How far is your work?

Person: Yes please. Can it also play the next episode of my podcast when it rings?
Assistant: I can't play a podcast with the alarm, sorry. I can use a gentle ringtone, if you like.
Person: That's fine. Thanks!

Ben was waiting in his taxi for a passenger, and he had a problem. His friend Sam was turning thirty-one on Sunday, and he had no idea what to buy. 'Gift ideas for a man who likes cooking,' he said to the assistant. It gave him three ideas: a good knife, a thin cookbook of quick meals, and a set of spices. Ben liked the cookbook. 'Try the market,' said the assistant. 'A stall near you sells books on Saturdays.' Ben asked it to set a reminder for Saturday morning and to save the date of Sam's birthday for next year. The assistant did both. When his passenger came, Ben put the phone away and started the engine, happy that the gift was sorted.

When you buy something online, a tracking number lets you see where the package is. The shop says when it will arrive, and each day the tracker shows the next step. People often ask, 'Where is my parcel?' or 'When will it come?' If the box is damaged, or a bottle leaked inside, they can ask for a refund. They say, 'Send it back' or 'I want my money back.' A refund can take up to a month to show up. Some people check the tracker every morning. A voice assistant can answer these questions and tell you the new delivery day.

Xiu was driving home when her head began to pound. She pulled over and said to the assistant, 'My head is killing me, and I've run out of pills.' The assistant understood. It said it could find a pharmacy and asked for her location. Xiu allowed it. The nearest pharmacy was two kilometres north, and it was open until nine. 'Take me there,' she said. The assistant started directions and spoke each turn clearly. At the pharmacy, she bought her medicine. The assistant then asked if she wanted a reminder to take the next dose, and she said yes, in four hours. Xiu drank some water and felt calmer. The drive home was slow, but she was safe.

Person: Good morning. Could you please help me with a sum? I just woke up and my head is foggy, and the dog spilled coffee over my notes, so I can't read them.
Assistant: Of course. What would you like me to work out?
Person: I think the main total was 230. Take away 45.
Assistant: 230 minus 45 is 185.
Person: Thank you. What is half of that?
Assistant: Half of 185 is 92.5.
Person: Great. Can you also write the answer on my paper notes?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't write on paper, but I can send the answer to your phone.
Person: Please do.

A baby has a rhythm of feeding times and nap times, and parents write it down to keep track. A baby monitor lets you hear or see a tiny sleeper from another room, even in fog or darkness. If the baby wakes, the monitor sounds an alert. Parents change the plan with simple words: 'Move the nap to two,' 'Feed her in an hour,' or 'Turn the monitor up.' Some say, 'Keep the sound low, she's asleep.' An assistant can set reminders for each feeding and nap so tired parents do not have to remember everything.

Bram worked in gardens all day, and tonight he wanted a nice dinner out. He said to the assistant, 'Book a table for two at the Italian place near the park, at seven. I don't want a seat near the door.' The assistant booked a table by the window and read out the details. 'Does the place have plants?' he asked. The assistant said the room was full of green plants and a red wall. Bram laughed. 'I don't understand the menu,' he said. The assistant read out the dishes in simple words and told him the pasta was the best. Bram chose it. He also asked for no onions, and the assistant added a note to the booking. He washed his hands and put on a clean shirt.

Tesfaye cooked in a busy kitchen all day, and now he wanted a short ride on his bike. He unplugged the battery charger and said to the assistant, 'Could you please find a bike route to the river? My legs are tired after work, so I would like one without big hills.' The assistant showed a flat path along the water. It was seven kilometres long. Time was tight, because the light would fade in an hour. 'How long will that take?' he asked. The assistant said about thirty minutes each way. Tesfaye checked the tyres, which felt firm, and rode off. He enjoyed the quiet path and was home before dark.

Yuri parked on the lawn behind his office, where the staff leave their cars when the lot is full. At six he walked out and could not remember which corner he parked at. He said to the assistant, 'Check my tyre pressure and tell me where I parked.' The assistant told him the car was on the north side of the lawn, and the front left tyre was a little low. Yuri found the car and filled the tyre at a petrol station. He had a fancy dinner that evening and wanted a shower first, so he drove home quickly. Before he went inside, he asked the assistant to remind him to check the tyres again on Friday. It did.

Person: Can the robot clean? Mum is at the theater and I want the house to be lovely when she comes back.
Assistant: Yes. Which room should it clean?
Person: The kitchen and the hall. But keep it quiet, the cat hurt his paw and is sleeping.
Assistant: Okay, I will use quiet mode. Should it clean all the floor or only some?

Assistant: Good. I will start with the half near the table, then the hall.
Person: Can it also wash the dishes?
Assistant: I'm sorry, the robot can only clean floors. I can't wash dishes.

Assistant: Okay, I will skip the garden room. What time should it start?
Person: After lunch, I think.
Assistant: Would one o'clock be good?
Person: Yes. It takes half an hour, doesn't it?
Assistant: Usually about that long for the rooms you named. Shall I start it tomorrow at one?
Person: Yes, dear. My flowers grow better when nothing bumps them.
Assistant: I will keep the robot away from them. It is set for tomorrow at one.

Callum was a retired teacher, and he liked his quiet street. One morning a loud noise came from the field. A cow had wandered onto Mill Road, and the neighbours began to shout. Callum took his phone and said, 'Post in the village group that a cow is loose on Mill Road.' Then he stopped. 'No, I mean Mill Lane, sorry.' The assistant fixed the post and sent it. Soon a farmer answered and said the cow was his. The assistant read the replies to Callum. The farmer thanked him, and the constant barking of the dogs slowly faded as the cow went home. Callum asked if there was a local event this weekend, and the assistant told him about the village fair.

An alarm wakes you at a time you pick, and a timer counts down from a number of minutes. In the kitchen, a timer tells you when the fruit pie is ready. Many alarms are automatic: they ring on weekdays and rest at the weekend. People change them with short words: 'Wake me at six,' 'Snooze ten minutes,' 'Make it ring later,' or 'Cancel tomorrow's alarm.' A watch you wear on your wrist can ring quietly so only you hear it. An assistant can set an alarm, change it, or turn it off when you say so.
